the use of the bioresorbable polymeric nanoparticles, which are functionalized with the α(5)/β(1) targeting peptide, PR-b, is a promising route to minimize the dose-limiting toxic side effects associated with the current approaches of cisplatin chemotherapy.

this work has developed and characterized a novel targeted delivery system that can deliver the anticancer drug, cisplatin, to cancer cells in a site-selective manner with minimal toxicity to healthy cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a bioresorbable, biocompatible, and biodegradable polymersome system that can be functionalized with a peptide ligand that is specific to the cancer cell type and is able to target the cancer cell with a payload of cisplatin.
we have developed an approach for site-selective delivery of cisplatine to cancer cells overexpressed with α(5) integrin.
the PR_b targeting peptide was able to improve cisplatin uptake in DLD-1 cells, which are known to express high levels of the α(5)-integrin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PR_b targeting peptide greatly improves the delivery of cisplatine to α(5)-integrin overexpressing cells and that the polymersomes are biodegradable, which is a desirable feature for the delivery of anticancer drugs.

we have demonstrated that we can use a bioresorbable polymer to make a drug carrier that can target cells that have high levels of integrin α5β1 and that this carrier can release the drug cisplatin inside of those cells.
bioresorbable polymer nanoparticles can be targeted to specific cell types using a peptide ligand, and this targeting can be achieved without using toxic catalysts or harsh reaction conditions.
